item: fts_status reports the full-text index's own population and names an index that is empty or whose tail is missing as unhealthy; the integrity report's delta can finally be non-zero
summary: Follow-on to the item 29 tests: a clear defect. article_fts is an external-content FTS5 table, so fts_status's health probe and count are answered from the articles table; measured after delete-all on a 300-article store: article_fts_docsize 0, fts_status healthy True, rows 300, ok. The integrity report's delta was articles minus that same count, so it was always 0. The Export lane's measurement found the same blind spot for a prefix index (some rows, not all; constructed, a torn copy or hand-made restore): boot skipped it, fts_status said healthy with rows equal to all articles, and search returned about half. NOW: fts_status step 4 reads, in ONE statement (one read snapshot), max(id) of articles, COUNT(*) of the shadow table article_fts_docsize and its max(id), inside one bounded block, and reports indexed_documents, indexed_status (ok, timed_out, error, skipped, unprobeable for a columnsize=0 build) and index_state: empty, partial (inferred) when the index's highest document id is below the highest article id, ends-agree otherwise (what was compared, not agreement and not a proof of completeness), None when unknown. Empty and partial set healthy False with fixed labels EmptyIndex and PartialIndex, which never replace an error the content count already named; nothing is repaired and no article is counted (the boot's refusal of the 74 s cold count stands, and the boot still skips a prefix index). One statement because separate reads cannot be ordered safely: ids are reused after the top articles are deleted, so a re-read after a delete and an ingest sees a new article under an old id and reads a fully indexed store as partial (an independent read reproduced it on the first version, which read the top id first and asked it again). The integrity block counts articles before it reads the index, keeps fts_rows, gains indexed_documents, indexed_status and index_state, and its delta is articles minus indexed_documents. Tests: 17 new functions (one parametrized twice) and 2 extended in tests/test_fts_status.py (whole, emptied, empty over no articles, tail missing then a hole after the next ingest, an index ahead of its articles, a reused id, a prefix of 10 of 20 with no count of articles run at the cursor, the three numbers in one statement, slow count, own deadline, failed read, earlier error kept, the verdict not replacing the count's error, columnsize=0, no index or backend); the Export lane's draft joined tests/test_repair_search_index.py under its name (a full rebuild that dies after two batches leaves the whole old index; an emptied index whose heal dies stays empty and the next boot fills it; a strict xfail that a boot repairs a prefix, which it does not by design; and fts_status naming that prefix); the new failure_text sink is registered in test_sink_sweep_records (3 to 4). RED WITHOUT: 13 mutants in fts_status and the integrity block red (step 4 never run: 19 tests; each verdict; the compare of the ends; the statement split in two; the deadline; the earlier error, twice) and a rebuild_index that commits per batch red in both Export tests. BYTES: the integrity fts block at indent 2 with 1048725 articles shrinks in every shape that existed: healthy 451 to 441, unprobeable 451 to 442, a 78-byte error label with a timed-out population 530 to 516, every longest value at once 535 to 523; the new empty and partial states are 445 and 464 and the new longest shape (a 78-byte count error beside a partial index) is 530. LIMITS: a hole in the middle or a missing head is not seen by the ends (only the integrity delta sees it), and a partial verdict closes at the next ingest, which turns the missing tail into a hole in the middle; an index that holds documents beyond the highest article id reads ends-agree; partial says nothing of how many are missing; the first build of an index on a store that already has articles reads empty until it is done; the integrity drift verdict does not read the fts block; the unprobeable build is hand-made in the test; the cold encrypted cost of the id lookups and the 1 M-article count were not measured here (Export measured 0.1 to 0.25 ms and 2.5 ms warm at 400,000); the interrupted mapping in salvage._raise_for_target stays a dead line.
